package_info.why_malicious: The report details a surge in phishing and malware campaigns exploiting COVID-19 themes, but does not identify any specific malicious software package, code, or library. The primary threats are social engineering attacks (phishing emails) that use pandemic-related lures to trick users into opening malicious attachments or clicking on links, rather than malicious code distributed via software packages.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing emails leveraging COVID-19 themes or impersonating government/health organizations to induce urgency or fear.
Emails prompting recipients to download attachments or click on links under the pretense of pandemic-related updates.
Use of sender addresses or display names mimicking trusted health or government entities.
file_indicators: Email attachments with COVID-19-themed filenames (e.g., COVID19-update.pdf, WHO-guidelines.docx, coronavirus-info.xls).
Attachment file types commonly used for malware delivery (e.g., .exe, .scr, .js, .docm, .xlsm) with pandemic-related names.
Links within emails pointing to domains that closely resemble or spoof legitimate health organizations (e.g., who-covid19-info.com, cdc-update.org).
network_indicators: Outbound connections to newly registered or suspicious domains containing COVID-19, corona, or health-related keywords.
Links to phishing sites impersonating WHO, CDC, or government portals, often using lookalike domains.
Observed traffic to IP addresses or domains flagged in threat intelligence feeds as associated with COVID-19-themed phishing.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor inbound email for COVID-19 or pandemic-related subject lines, attachments, or embedded links, especially those impersonating trusted organizations. Use sandboxing to analyze attachments and URLs for malicious behavior. Flag emails with mismatched sender domains, display names, or those requesting sensitive information under urgent pandemic pretexts. Integrate threat intelligence feeds to block or alert on known phishing domains and update detection rules for pandemic-themed lures. Employ domain age and reputation checks for links in emails, and alert on newly registered or suspicious domains.
